panels.rationale: Single-panel clinical photograph of a real patient showing bilateral pitting dorsal hand edema with symmetrical synovitis of the wrists and MCP joints; the caption explicitly attributes the presentation to RS3PE syndrome ('Clinical presentation of RS3PE syndrome. Bilateral pitting edema of the hands with symmetrical synovitis involving the wrists and metacarpophalangeal joints'), matching the classic boxing-glove hand edema phenotype. Prior caption triage also classified it as a real patient RS3PE clinical photo with no third-party indication. Skin is adequately lit and shows medium tone with chronic sun-damaged elderly hands; no ethnicity or specific patient age stated in caption or in-text, so ethnicity is null and age group is inferred as older adult from visible elderly hands plus in-text statement that RS3PE typically affects elderly individuals.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a clinical photograph showing edema and erythema of the hands and fingers, consistent with the clinical presentation of rs3pe. B: Panel B is an ultrasound of the arm demonstrating fluid retention and synovitis in the biceps and joint sheaths, indicative of active rs3pe inflammation.
panels.attribution_text: Ohmura et al. Case Report: Resolution of remitting seronegative symmetrical synovitis with pitting edema during nivolumab therapy for gastric cancer.. Frontiers in oncology 2023. doi:10.3389/fonc.2023.1260818. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Edema of both fingers and the dorsa of both hands and erythema on the dorsal sides of the fingers (A). On ultrasonographic examination, fluid retention around the biceps, synovitis of the biceps, and synovitis of the joint synovium and tendon sheath synovium are observed (B).
in_text_mentions: During the administration of nivolumab, edema of both fingers and the dorsa of both hands appeared in April 2018 ( Figure 1 ), and pitting edema of both lower legs deteriorated. Erythema also appeared on the dorsal sides of the fingers. On ultrasonographic examination, fluid retention around the biceps, synovitis of the biceps, and synovitis of the joint synovium and tendon sheath synovium were observed ( Figure 1 ). There were no abnormalities in thyroid hormone levels or the blood coagulation system. C-reactive protein was as high as 6.75 mg/dL, and rheumatoid factor was negative (8 U/mL). S
